items.title: How different judgment strategies affect accuracy in generative AI text discrimination: BERT-based clustering and hierarchical Bayesian logistic regression
items.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs)-generated texts become increasingly similar to human writing. The purpose of this study was to examine (1) how individuals distinguish between human-written and LLM-generated texts, focusing on their judgment strategies; (2) the relationship between judgment strategies and detection accuracy; and (3) the interaction effects of gender, age, and frequency of large language model (LLM) use. Methods Participants were asked to judge whether the given texts (e.g., public comments) were written by LLMs or humans and to explain their reasoning using open-ended questions. The public comments were written by humans and generated using seven LLMs (ChatGPT [4o and o1], Claude3.5, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Llama3.1, and Perplexity). First, we classified participants’ explanations of reasoning related to judgments into types using BERT-based clustering (i.e., Sentence-BERT and hierarchical cluster analysis). Results BERT-based clustering suggested four interpretable clusters. Based on their characteristic patterns, we interpreted these clusters as four hypothetical judgment strategy types and tentatively proposed that they form a conceptual continuum: (1) Unsubstantiated intuition, (2) Stylistic-Cue, (3) Syntactic-Cue, and (4) Higher-Order Pattern Recognition (HOPR). A hierarchical Bayesian logistic regression analysis revealed that the detection accuracy varied across judgment types, with the HOPR type achieving relatively higher performance than the other strategy types, although its detection accuracy remained near the chance level. Additionally, we identified interaction effects between strategy type and gender; only female participants who used the HOPR strategy showed lower detection accuracy than male participants, although the qualitative interpretation of this difference warrants further empirical investigation. Conclusion These findings emphasize the role of judgment strategies and individual differences in discriminating between human and LLM-generated content.

items.title: How human–AI collaboration event strength shapes information security behavior: evidence from a University in Shanghai
items.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into higher education learning contexts, university students receive technological support while also facing new information security risks. However, existing research has paid limited attention to how the event characteristics of human-AI collaboration are associated with university students' information security behavior and to the psychological processes underlying these relationships. Drawing on event system theory, this study develops a dual pathway model to examine how human-AI collaboration event strength, reflected in event novelty, event disruption, and event criticality, is associated with information security behavior among university students through security vigilance and cognitive overload. Methods Data were collected from students at a university in Shanghai using a three-wave time-lagged survey design, yielding 351 valid responses. Results The results show that event novelty, event disruption, and event criticality are positively associated with security vigilance and cognitive overload. Security vigilance is positively associated with information security behavior, whereas cognitive overload is negatively associated with information security behavior. Further analyses indicate that these event strength attributes generate positive indirect effects through security vigilance and negative indirect effects through cognitive overload. Discussion This study explains information security behavior during university students' use of artificial intelligence from an event-strength perspective and provides a more nuanced understanding of the underlying psychological processes. The findings provide a theoretical basis for universities to refine guidelines for artificial intelligence use, strengthen information security education, and optimize the design of human-AI collaborative learning.

items.title: How media narratives shape public sentiment toward electric micromobility: Stronger effects for e-scooters than e-bikes
items.abstract: Public sentiment toward electric micromobility, particularly e-scooters and e-bikes, is increasingly shaping safety debates and regulatory responses; yet, these attitudes and perceptions have not been systematically evaluated within a unified framework, nor is it clear to what extent they reflect stable judgments versus sensitivity to external narratives. This study addresses these gaps by quantifying public sentiment toward e-bikes and e-scooters and evaluating their responsiveness to controlled negative media narrative exposure. A unified survey framework was developed to enable consistent evaluation, combining statement-based measures with image-based scenario assessments. Two complementary studies were conducted with Australian participants. Study 1 (N = 1027) established baseline sentiment in the absence of media exposure, and Study 2 (N = 1025) examined how responses shift following controlled exposure to negative news headlines. The results showed that public sentiment is multi-dimensional and mixed. While both modes received moderate recognition in terms of sustainability and legitimacy, practical acceptance remained lower, particularly for e-scooters. Exposure to negative media narratives produced broader and more consistent shifts toward less favorable sentiments for e-scooters, especially in perceptions of rider behavior and public-space interaction, whereas e-bike responses remained comparatively stable and more robust to media narrative exposure. In contrast, evaluations of concrete negative situations showed no systematic change following exposure, indicating that these evaluations are grounded in situational interpretation rather than external framing. The findings suggest that public sentiment should be used cautiously to inform policy development. While consistent concerns linked to observable safety issues justify targeted interventions, broader sentiment shifts may reflect narrative influence rather than actual conditions. Effective policy should therefore be informed not only by public sentiment but also by objective evidence on behavior, exposure, and risk.

items.title: How Middle-Power Coordination Can Shape Frontier AI Governance
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) middle powers are already shaping international AI governance, from the Bletchley, Seoul, Paris, and India AI Summits to initiatives such as the Hiroshima AI Process and the International Network for Advanced AI Measurement, Evaluation and Science (formerly the International Network of AI Safety Institutes). Their diplomatic, institutional, regulatory, economic, and technical strengths, however, remain unevenly distributed. “Shared sovereignty,” a strategic pathway identified by Chatham House, offers one way for AI middle powers to pool complementary strengths with like-minded countries and build collective leverage around international AI red lines, particularly limits on unacceptable AI uses and behaviours. This inquiry asks when and how coordination can turn unevenly distributed national capabilities into collective leverage. It examines six middle powers beyond Europe: Brazil, Canada, India, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore, across four episodes of international AI governance. The analysis compares different coordination configurations, the mechanisms and instruments they use, and the conditions under which they generate collective leverage. The findings show that broad participation does not necessarily produce sustained coordination. Middle powers bring complementary strengths, but no single country consistently combines the capabilities needed to influence technical, regulatory, institutional, and diplomatic domains. Coordination generates leverage when these strengths are converted into mechanisms and instruments that produce observable effects. The Hiroshima AI Process Reporting Framework illustrates this dynamic. Developed with support from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) to monitor voluntary adoption of the Hiroshima AI Process International Code of Conduct, the framework translates international commitments into structured reporting on risk management, incident reporting, and information sharing. Its adoption by AI developers created a common reporting structure and generated comparable information on how companies were implementing the Code. This episode suggests that the effects a coordination instrument produces, and the governance arrangements that enable them, can matter as much as its level of institutionalisation when developing mechanisms for behavioural red lines. The analysis identifies five conditions that enable coordination to translate into collective leverage: relational coordination, capability mobilisation, institutional output, governance location, and observable effect. For middle powers, these findings point to five practical priorities: (i) use international and plurilateral forums strategically to identify partners and build support for shared governance objectives; (ii) connect complementary capabilities and authorities across points of interdependence in the AI stack, from model development and evaluation to deployment and risk management, around specific risks and potential red lines; (iii) convert shared commitments into workable assessment, reporting, and response mechanisms; (iv) target governance locations where authority, incentives, and implementation capacity can influence developer behaviour; and (v) assess whether these mechanisms produce observable effects by strengthening shared safety evaluation, monitoring, and technical capacity.

items.title: How the Diagnosticity of AI-Based Sustainability Information Relates to Sustainable Consumption Behavior: The Roles of Perceived Consumer Effectiveness and Environmental Self-Identity
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to provide sustainability-related information to consumers. Yet, its relevance to sustainable consumption may depend less on the presence of AI itself than on whether the information it provides is perceived as useful for decision-making. This study examines how the perceived diagnosticity of AI-based sustainability information is associated with sustainable consumption behavior through perceived consumer effectiveness (PCE) and environmental self-identity. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework and the information diagnosticity perspective, the study proposes an information–agency–identity–behavior pathway in which diagnostic sustainability information is associated with stronger perceptions of the environmental consequentiality of individual choices, which are subsequently associated with environmental self-identity and sustainable consumption behavior. Survey data were collected from 313 South Korean adult consumers with recent experience using AI-based services to obtain or evaluate sustainability-related information, and the proposed relationships were examined using structural equation modeling. The results supported the hypothesized associations: perceived diagnosticity was positively associated with PCE (β = 0.582), PCE was positively associated with environmental self-identity (β = 0.638), and environmental self-identity was positively associated with sustainable consumption behavior (β = 0.597). The sequential indirect association through PCE and environmental self-identity was significant (indirect effect = 0.214, 95% CI [0.145, 0.298]), while the direct association between perceived diagnosticity and sustainable consumption behavior also remained significant (β = 0.157, p = 0.008), consistent with complementary mediation. These findings are consistent with the proposed sequence but do not establish the temporal ordering between PCE and environmental self-identity. These findings highlight the decision relevance of AI-provided sustainability information and distinguish agency-related cognition from identity-related self-concept as complementary psychological mechanisms that may jointly relate information appraisal to sustainable consumption. The findings further suggest that the sustainability relevance of AI may depend not merely on technological adoption, but on whether AI-mediated information helps consumers evaluate environmental alternatives, recognize the significance of their choices, and connect environmentally responsible consumption with their self-concept.

items.title: How trust shapes human reliance on AI decision support in healthcare: A simulation-based behavioral study
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) based decision support systems are increasingly used in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, making it important to understand how trust relates to the use of AI recommendations. Although trust can support effective human–AI collaboration, miscalibrated trust may contribute to inappropriate recommendation acceptance and reduced decision performance. This study examined associations among perceived AI performance, trust, AI recommendation acceptance, and decision accuracy under different levels of AI reliability. In a simulation-based experiment, 100 medical students completed clinical decision-making tasks with AI assistance under high- and low-reliability conditions. Perceived AI performance and trust were measured after each block, while recommendation acceptance and decision accuracy were recorded at the trial level. Mixed-effects models showed that perceived AI performance was positively associated with trust. Higher trust was associated with greater overall acceptance of AI recommendations and greater acceptance of incorrect recommendations. Conversely, higher trust was associated with lower odds of rejecting correct recommendations, indicating more frequent rejection at lower trust. Greater misalignment between normalized trust and objective AI reliability was associated with lower decision accuracy. These findings indicate that calibrated trust is important for effective AI-assisted decision making. They also support the development and evaluation of AI interfaces that communicate reliability and uncertainty to help users align trust with system capability.

items.title: HRI, Culture, and Social Anxiety
items.abstract: Culture and social anxiety are among the human factors influencing the social acceptance of robots. In this chapter, research results are presented based on comparisons among nations conducted by the author’s research group, consisting of those about attitudes toward robots, assumptions about and images of robots, Frankenstein Syndrome, and roboethics. Then, an overview of social anxiety-related research in the field of human–robot interaction (HRI) is provided, regarding on fear of negative evaluation and gaze impact, impact of social anxiety on anxiety and tension during interactions with robots, and effects of social anxiety on robot preference in dialogue situations. Finally, the possibility of interaction effects between cultural factors and social anxiety in HRI is discussed and some future research directions are proposed.

items.title: Human factor H-related protein 5 modulates the classical and lectin complement pathways on selected host ligands
items.abstract: Abstract C4b-binding protein (C4BP) and factor H (FH) are the main soluble negative regulators of the classical/lectin (CP/LP) and alternative (AP) complement pathways, respectively. They do not only act in solution but also interact with host ligands such as C-reactive protein (CRP) and extracellular matrix proteins to control complement activation on surfaces. Factor H-related (FHR) proteins share structural homology with FH and modulate complement activation by competing with FH for ligands and enhancing AP activation. Due to their overlapping ligand profile with both FH and C4BP, we studied the potential effect of FHR-1, FHR-2, and FHR-5 on C4BP function and on CP/LP activation. Both FHR-1 and FHR-5 inhibited C4BP binding to surface-bound CRP and osteoadherin. This translated to reduced surface cofactor activity of C4BP on CRP in the presence of FHR-5. Unexpectedly, FHR-5 inhibited CP activation, indicated by decreased C3- and C4-fragments deposition from serum, which was due to inhibition of C1q binding on CRP and osteoadherin. FHR-1 and FHR-2 did not influence CP activation. In addition, FHR-5 inhibited LP activation by competing with ficolin-2 and ficolin-3. In conclusion, our results revealed a novel role of FHR-5 in modulating the activity of the complement CP and LP.

items.title: Human Factors in Robotics for Motor Rehabilitation, Assistance, and Prosthetics
items.abstract: Among the challenges in biomedical robotics, assisting and restoring motor skills is a priority to enable individuals with impairments to perform activities of daily living (ADLs). Robots can enhance human mobility and interaction capabilities through solutions tailored to individual skills, limitations, and goals in specific contexts. For rehabilitation, end-effector robots and exoskeletons are often programmed to guide users in exercises designed to restore motor functions after severe incidents, such as strokes, or in cases of chronic and degenerative conditions. These devices can also be integrated into telerehabilitation systems. Assistive robots, on the other hand, improve the quality of life for individuals whose impairments cannot be fully addressed through therapy, such as those due to aging. Devices like robotic arms, wheelchairs, walkers, and exoskeletons support ADLs and even facilitate social interactions through telepresence systems. Bionic prostheses, designed for limb replacement in cases of amputation or agenesis, could achieve a high level of embodiment–allowing users to perceive the prosthesis as part of their body. This need for a better integration between humans and robots exemplifies challenges common to all three domains. This chapter introduces fundamental aspects of cognitive ergonomics and human factors that designers, clinicians, and users must consider when using rehabilitative, assistive, or prosthetic systems. The ultimate goal is to provide a ‘truly’ human-centered motor assistance, and recovery, through robotic systems.

items.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Pedagogy and Ethical Assessment in GenAI-Integrated Education
items.abstract: This chapter proposes that human-AI cooperation in learning analytics and evaluation is not a neutral technological advancement, but rather a normative design problem. In order to provide validity, reliability, equity, privacy, and academic integrity as hard design constraints, it integrates concepts from psychometrics, algorithmic fairness, data protection legislation, socio-technical systems theory, and critical pedagogy. In order to mitigate the risks posed by generative AI to authorship, inclusivity, and trust, the chapter presents a risk and harm taxonomy, a privacy by design control matrix, and discipline-aware evaluation redesign patterns. Procurement, model stewardship, and quality assurance are reframed as cyclical, data-informed procedures that divide supervision among institutional actors via a staged governance and evidence planner. The chapter presents a justice-focused framework where AI serves as a contestable and augmentative partner that expands educational intelligence while still being answerable to students, teachers, and democratic communities.

items.title: Human-AI Work Redistribution Across the Software Development Life Cycle: A Socio-Technical Study of Indonesian Developers
items.abstract: AI Coding Assistants are becoming increasingly integrated into software development, changing not only how developers perform their tasks but also how humans and AI share responsibilities. However, how this redistribution of work occurs across the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates how responsibilities are distributed between developers and AI across SDLC activities, how these changes affect software engineering workflows and developer roles, and which socio-technical factors influence this process. Semi-structured interviews with seven software professionals in Indonesia were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The results identify three patterns of human-AI work redistribution: AI-delegated, AI-augmented, and human-controlled work. AI contributes more substantially to structured, repetitive, and relatively verifiable activities, particularly code generation, debugging, testing, and documentation. In contrast, requirements analysis, architectural decisions, security assessment, and release approval remain largely under human control because they require contextual understanding, professional judgment, and accountability. The findings also indicate a shift in developer responsibilities. This redistribution depends on developer experience, AI literacy, trust, model capability, task complexity, security requirements, team practices, and organizational policies. Drawing on socio-technical systems theory and activity theory, the study develops an empirically grounded Human-AI Work Redistribution Model that conceptualizes AI-assisted software engineering as a selective redistribution of responsibilities rather than uniform automation across the SDLC.

items.title: Human-Centered Robotics for Surgery
items.abstract: Surgical ergonomics is influenced by many aspects associated with posture, vision, hand motion, and haptic feedback. Specific ergonomics aspects can induce long-term effects in the surgeon directly affecting the performance. One of the major disadvantages of Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS) remains the non-ergonomic design of the entire surgical environment. This condition results in a significant reduction in the quality of interventions and discomfort for the medical operator. Modern teleoperated surgical robots offer an optimized console, in which the surgeon can operate in a seated position with specific arm support and a 3D view of the operating site. The da Vinci surgical console offers ergonomic improvements over standard endoscopic surgery. Modern robotic platforms stand beyond the da Vinci System, offering more advanced ergonomic solutions in terms of haptic feedback and visual perception. Due to the introduction of more advanced technology, surgery has changed, resulting in increased system complexity at the technical, human and organizational levels, which may lead to higher variability of patient outcomes due to new error pathways. Adopting a proactive approach enables the prior identification of critical factors and the design of safer socio-technical systems, thanks to a multi-level perspective. This chapter addresses the fundamental elements of surgical ergonomics, considering the factors that affect performance and healthiness during traditional procedures, with specific reference to MIS and microsurgery. This baseline is then compared to the use of surgical robots by evaluating the effect of design decisions on operator ergonomics. In addition, studies propose proactive methodologies that assess the personal and organizational factors of surgical performance in this complex socio-technical system.

items.title: Human–Robot Interaction and Ergonomics
items.abstract: Robots in the workplace are becoming a familiar sight. Hence, they have become the focus of debates and research on workplace ergonomics. While this emerging technology holds great promise to improve environments, this can only be achieved through the intentional application of ergonomic principles. Physical, cognitive and organizational ergonomics must be considered when talking about human-robot interaction (HRI) in a work environment. This chapter presents fundamentals on both human-robot interaction and ergonomics. This includes key topics such as potential roles of humans in HRI, interaction design and interfaces. Furthermore, it presents key domains of HRI and the emerging perspectives in research and application. It underscores the importance of an interdisciplinary approach in assessing the impact of robotics on humans and emphasizes the need for a human-centered design philosophy when developing innovative robotic systems.

items.title: Human–Robot Interaction in Industrial Contexts
items.abstract: Technological advances in industrial robotics have significantly changed modern working environments, enabling greater autonomy, flexibility and productivity. Here the emergence of advanced robots designed for direct interaction with humans play a substantial role. By integrating emerging technologies such as AI, machine learning, and sophisticated interaction design, advanced robots are reshaping industries. All while increasing efficiency and customization and remaining cost-effective. Despite their benefits, the use of robotic systems also brings challenges, particularly in the area of occupational safety and health. After an overview of the evolution of different robotic systems, a description of industrial work tasks, related working conditions and highlighted risk and opportunities associated with automation, this chapter examines key safety factors that are essential for close human–robot interaction and assesses their impact on workers. Two case studies illustrate how the practical application of advanced robotic systems in industrial settings affects workplace dynamics. The chapter further highlights the role of worker expectations and experience in relation to advanced robotics. By combining empirical evidence with real-world applications, this chapter underscores the importance of adaptable, user-friendly robotic systems that prioritize worker well-being alongside operational efficiency. In doing so, it contributes to the broader dialogue on sustainable, ergonomic innovation in the workplace and highlights the critical role of human-centered design in the future of industrial robotics.

items.title: Humans and Robots in Agriculture
items.abstract: Research in agricultural robotics has garnered increasing attention over the past decade. Simultaneously, Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) has emerged as a possible solution to increase automation and reduce the lack of human labor in the field. This chapter presents a study of research trends in HRI focusing on Artificial Intelligence (AI), human factors, and ergonomics in collaborative agricultural tasks. For example, we talk about the importance of robotics and the application of the different AI-based methods for HRI in field applications. Moreover, we emphasize situation awareness, stress, sleepiness, sleep quality, and distraction. We also explore various crucial and innovative topics related to HRI in agriculture, including safety, human factors, ergonomics, awareness, productivity, and management. This analysis shows that HRI paradigms can be effectively applied in agricultural applications, yielding promising production, safety, and farm management benefits, such as increasing productivity and reducing human workload.

items.title: Hybrid Residual SARIMAX-XGBoost for Provincial Rice Production Forecasting in Indonesia: A Systematic Literature Review and Conceptual Framework for Food Policy Decision Support
items.abstract: This study contributes a systematic literature review and conceptual framework for provincial rice production forecasting in Indonesia by integrating residual-based hybrid modelling, explainability, and food policy decision support. A total of 60 articles published between 2023 and 2026 were selected from 124 initial records identified from six academic search sources: ScienceDirect/Elsevier, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, MDPI journals, Scopus/Crossref tracing, and Google Scholar/manual tracking, using a PRISMA-style screening process. The review synthesizes evidence across rice production forecasting, crop-yield forecasting, hybrid machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and decision-support-oriented forecasting. The literature findings show that recent studies increasingly use agricultural statistics, climate variables, remote sensing, UAV imagery, crop-model outputs, machine learning, and deep learning. However, the reviewed studies rarely integrate province-aware determinants, residual-based model decomposition, time-aware validation, residual-level explainability, and DSS-ready policy outputs within a single framework. Based on this gap, the study proposes a conceptual Hybrid Residual SARIMAX-XGBoost framework. SARIMAX is positioned to model temporal, seasonal, autoregressive, and exogenous baseline patterns, while XGBoost learns nonlinear residual structures. SHAP is positioned as an explanation layer for interpreting forecast adjustments rather than as causal evidence. The proposed framework remains conceptual and requires future empirical validation using Indonesian provincial rice production data. This review provides theoretical contributions to hybrid forecasting literature and practical implications for information systems, decision support, and public-sector food policy planning.

items.title: Identifying technological problems and exploring potential solutions to support R&D: Tech-mining with multi-LLM applications
items.abstract: The shortening of technology lifecycles and growing technological complexity have made the rapid identification of technical problems and exploration of solutions a critical challenge. Patent analysis can serve as a crucial tool for supporting R&D activities by extracting problem–solution pairs from patent documents. However, current patent analysis methods have several limitations. They focus primarily on extracting technical problems from patents without providing a systematic framework for transforming fragmented problems into comprehensive technological intelligence. Moreover, they remain heavily dependent on technical experts, with supervised learning models struggling to achieve the expected performance on unseen data, which is a particularly critical issue given the accelerating technological change. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a systematic framework that converts fragmented technical problems into actionable technological intelligence. The framework performs target–symptom decomposition, inter-problem causal analysis, and solution portfolio development, while employing a multi-large-language-model (multi-LLM) architecture with few-shot learning capabilities to reduce the dependence on technical experts and enhance analytical reliability. A case study of hydrogen storage technology with cross-domain demonstrations in the semiconductor and biopharmaceutical fields demonstrates that the framework can systematically identify technical problems, trace their root causes, and explore potential solutions to support R&D planning with improved cost efficiency and domain-independent applicability.

items.title: IMAGING EXAMS IN SUPPORT AND DIAGNOSIS OF DENTAL PROCEDURES
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the role of imaging exams in supporting diagnosis and guiding clinical and forensic procedures in contemporary dentistry. The methodology used was an integrative literature review, with searches conducted in Scielo, Lilacs, PubMed, and BVS databases, covering publications from 2022 to 2026. Twelve scientific articles were selected, directly addressing the use of imaging techniques such as conventional radiography, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), digital scanning, and emerging methods like virtopsy. The main results show that the appropriate use of these exams provides more accurate diagnoses, greater treatment predictability, and reduced risks in clinical and surgical procedures. Additionally, they demonstrate the relevance of imaging in forensic dentistry, significantly contributing to human identification. The integration of imaging technologies with planning software, 3D printing, and artificial intelligence enhances the quality of dental care. It is concluded that imaging exams have evolved from complementary tools to fundamental pillars of evidence-based dentistry, requiring technical expertise, continuous learning, and ethical responsibility from professionals in the face of technological advances.

items.title: Immersive innovation
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of advanced technologies, specifically the metaverse, is driving significant changes in supply chain management (SCM). This chapter showcases the rapid evolution of these advanced technologies, which mainly focus on the metaverse and its transformative impact on SCM. It explores how the integration of cutting-edge technologies such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), extended reality (XR), blockchain, machine learning, and artificial intelligence (AI) transforms traditional SCM structures and processes. Using these digital tools and techniques, the supply chain can achieve transparency, visibility, enhanced efficiency, and greater operational capacity; improve collaboration across stakeholders; and increase resilience in the face of disruption. Apart from these significant advantages, industries also face several challenges, such as high implementation costs, data privacy concerns, technological readiness gaps, and stakeholder resistance. This chapter also uncovers evolving trends linking the metaverse with the sustainability agenda and advanced AI capabilities, pointing toward a future where a hyperconnected, autonomous, and socially responsible supply chain operates in immersive digital environments. This comprehensive chapter provides detailed insights, information, and strategic, managerial, operational, and technological aspects to industrialists, managers, policymakers, and scholars for metaverse adoption in SCM, also offering a valuable foundation for both future academic and practical applications in the supply chain field.

items.title: Impact of Aggregation on the Immunogenicity of Therapeutic Recombinant Biological Products
items.abstract: Background: Therapeutic recombinant biological products are essential in modern medicine, but their immunogenicity remains a major concern for both clinical safety and therapeutic efficacy. Protein aggregation may occur during manufacturing, storage, transportation, and administration, potentially increasing immune recognition. Here, we have reviewed the mechanisms underlying aggregation-associated immunogenicity and summarized strategies for mitigating the associated risks. Methods: We integrated published evidence on therapeutic recombinant proteins, monoclonal antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates, peptide and glycoprotein hormones, and recombinant blood products. We focused on aggregation-induced structural changes, immune activation pathways, differences among product types and aggregation states, and approaches for controlling aggregation and mitigating immunogenicity. Results: Protein aggregation creates or reveals neoepitopes by disrupting the native conformational state, exposing previously buried hydrophobic regions, and generating nonnative interfaces. Aggregates may further promote innate and adaptive immune responses through repetitive epitope presentation, pattern-recognition receptor signaling, complement activation, cytokine release, dendritic-cell maturation, enhanced antigen presentation, and B-cell receptor cross-linking, ultimately increasing the likelihood of anti-drug antibody formation. Aggregate size and morphology, protein characteristics, formulation, storage conditions, administration route, and other biological factors influence the immunogenic potential of aggregates. Thus, effective risk reduction requires integrated control strategies, including molecular and structural optimization, formulation design, manufacturing-process control, appropriate storage and transportation, and sensitive analytical monitoring. Emerging artificial-intelligence approaches may further facilitate the prediction and design of low-immunogenicity biologics. Conclusions: Protein aggregation is a multifactorial determinant of immunogenicity. Controlling aggregation throughout the product lifecycle is essential to reduce immune-mediated risks and maintain safety, stability, and efficacy of therapeutic recombinant biological products.

items.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Recruitment and Selection
items.abstract: Recruitment has always involved a mix of judgment and administration. Recruiters read applications, compare experience with job requirements, arrange interviews, and try to make a fair decision within a limited time. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools now assist with some of these tasks. They can sort resumes, match skills to vacancies, answer routine questions, and help schedule interviews. These uses may save time, but they also raise questions that cannot be answered by speed alone: are suitable candidates being identified, do applicants understand how they are assessed, and can the process disadvantage particular groups? This paper proposes a study of AI use in recruitment and selection, focusing on recruitment efficiency, perceived fairness, candidate experience, and the role of human review. A mixed-methods design is proposed. A questionnaire would gather responses from HR professionals, recruiters, job seekers, and employees, while interviews with a smaller group of HR professionals would provide more detailed examples. Academic publications and institutional reports would be used to frame the study. The paper does not present completed survey findings; its hypotheses and sample plan are proposals to be tested. The intended contribution is a practical, balanced account of how organizations can assess AI recruitment tools without assuming that automation is automatically faster, fairer, or more accurate

items.title: IMPACT OF MOTIVATION ON TEACHERS' JOB PERFORMANCE IN NIGER STATE, NIGERIA
items.abstract: This study investigated the impact of motivation on teachers' job performance in Niger State, Nigeria, using two dimensions of motivation, namely: intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation. Extrinsic motivation was conceptualized broadly in this study to capture both the material and structural incentives that an employer provides, such as salary, promotion, and recognition, and the physical and social conditions under which teaching and learning occur, such as classroom facilities, supervisory support, and school climate, consistent with the hygiene component of Herzberg's two factor theory. Intrinsic motivation on the other hand refers to motivation that originates internally in the form of a person's interests and goals. The study adopted a quantitative, cross sectional survey design. The total population of the study consisted of 6200 teachers obtained from the 25 Local Government Areas of Niger State distributed in the 3 senatorial districts of Niger-East, Niger-North and Niger-West. A multi stage sampling technique was adopted: the first stage involved stratifying the twenty-five local government areas by senatorial district, the second stage involved the random selection of a proportionate number of schools within each stratum, and the third stage involved the simple random selection of individual teacher respondents within the selected schools. The sample size was determined using the Taro Yamane formula, expressed as n = N / (1 + N(e)²), where n represents the required sample size, N represents the target population, and e represents the margin of error, set conventionally at 0.05 (Yamane, 1967). Applying this formula to the population of six thousand two hundred teachers yields a computed sample size of approximately three hundred and eighty (380) respondents. The instrument used for data collection produced a reliability index of 0.75. The research questions were answered using descriptive statistics, including mean, standard deviation and frequencies, alongside inferential statistics, specifically multiple regression analysis, to test the two null hypotheses at 0.05 level of confidence corresponding to the two motivational dimensions. The findings of the study indicated that both dimensions of motivation exert a positive and statistically significant impact on teachers' job performance, with extrinsic motivation, inclusive of the work environment, showing the strongest predictive weight. The study concludes that a deliberate, balanced motivational policy that addresses intrinsic fulfilment alongside extrinsic motivation-material incentives, the physical teaching environment; is necessary to sustain teachers’ job performance in Niger State. Recommendations are offered for the State Ministry of Education and the Universal Basic Education Board as well as School Managers/Administrators.

items.title: Implementing and Scaling Artificial Intelligence in Low-Resourced Radiation Oncology: A Systematic Review of Deployments
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to address workforce shortages and workflow inefficiencies in radiation oncology, particularly in low-resourced settings where limited specialist capacity constrains access to care. This systematic review evaluated AI deployments in radiation oncology in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and assessed readiness for safe implementation and scale-up. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, six databases were searched from January 2000 through December 2025. Eligible studies were classified using a radiation oncology-specific integration spectrum (Levels 0-4) and evaluated for workflow integration, validation, deployment, and governance characteristics. Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Two studies (11.1%) focused on readiness or governance without clinical AI deployment (Level 0), nine (50.0%) reported task-level applications (Level 1), six (33.3%) demonstrated clinician-supervised workflow integration (Level 2), and one (5.6%) reported cross-stage workflow orchestration (Level 3). No study provided sufficient evidence for classification as Level 4 operation. Validation was predominantly retrospective, and continuous performance monitoring was not reported. AI deployment in LMIC radiation oncology remains concentrated at early stages of integration. This pattern reflects not a lack of innovation, but constraints in validation, workflow maturity, infrastructure, and governance. Safe and scalable deployment will require coordinated advances across these domains.

items.title: IMPROVING THE ADMINISTRATIVE AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK FOR DIGITAL ADMINISTRATIVE DECISION-MAKING IN PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION
items.abstract: This article examines the legal nature of digital administrative decisions emerging in the process of digitalizing public administration, the administrative and legal framework governing their adoption, and issues related to safeguarding citizens’ rights and legitimate interests. The development of digital government systems, the automation of administrative functions performed by public authorities, the interoperability of information systems, and the use of artificial intelligence technologies are giving rise to new forms of decision-making in public administration. In this regard, the article substantiates the inadequacy of mechanically transferring traditional administrative procedures into the digital environment. It analyzes the current legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan, particularly the Laws “On Administrative Procedures,” “On Electronic Government,” and “On Personal Data,” as well as newly adopted regulatory legal acts concerning the development of digital government and artificial intelligence. The article puts forward proposals addressing the legality, reasoned justification, transparency, human review, and accountability of digital administrative decisions.

items.title: Information shock: how AI demands an evolution of information science
items.abstract: Purpose This paper argues that AI authoring is prompting an Information Shock and a new information science. The shock is not a matter of increased volume and variable quality of AI-produced information. It comes as generative AI creates a new kind of author that dissolves the document, the field’s organizing unit. This forces a reconstitution of tools, literacies and identity. Design/methodology/approach The paper applies a conceptual framework drawn from the history of Information Shocks, tracing how disruptions from cuneiform to post-World War II research data forced the field to rebuild around new objects and practices. AI is analyzed against that pattern. Findings AI produces two modes of authorship: document-like objects that enter existing infrastructures, and transactional, co-authored exchanges with no stable unit to catalog, retrieve, cite or verify. The second mode renders AI literacy inadequate, even in its current forms, because they presuppose an identifiable object and human interlocutors. Anticipated changes reach professional identity, tools, intellectual property and education. Research limitations/implications The argument is theoretical and prospective, and some anticipated changes remain speculative. The Information Shock outlined is anticipated to have major impacts for librarians and information professionals moving forward. Originality/value The paper offers a historically grounded distinction between document-producing and transactional AI authorship, arguing that AI is pushing the exchange to take the mediating position that the field has long held.

items.title: Informing users about LLMs' environmental costs encourages ethical consumption
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming deeply embedded in everyday human-AI interaction. However, the environmental costs associated with using those tools remain elusive. Here, we address the question of whether providing users with information about the environmental costs of using LLMs tempers their use. Such information highlights an ethical tension: acting pro-environmentally requires people to forgo some of the benefits AI tools provide. We study how people solve this trade-off in tasks that are relatively easy to tackle without using LLMs and further assess if the impact of providing such information has a stronger effect on people who have stronger environmental concerns. In two preregistered experiments (total N = 1,200), we studied participants’ use of ChatGPT in a text-editing task after they learned about the tool’s environmental costs. Results revealed that (i) raising awareness of ChatGPT’s environmental costs reduced its use and usage volume; (ii) interacting with a sycophantic model, one that encourages continuous use, did not attenuate the awareness effect, although it led to greater overall use; and (iii) raising awareness was especially effective among people with high environmental concerns. The findings highlight how raising awareness concerning LLM’s environmental costs can encourage responsible consumption.

items.title: Innovative Job Performance in Digitally Enabled Workplaces: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Synthesis of Individual-Level Innovative Work Behavior
items.abstract: Innovative job performance (IJP) and innovative work behavior (IWB) are examined across distinct leadership, work-design, motivational, knowledge-sharing, and digital-work literatures. This review combines systematic full-text screening, bibliometric mapping, and a Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) synthesis to examine the individual-level evidence. The documented Scopus search of 19 September 2026 returned 23,225 records before database filters; 182 journal articles published in 2023–2026 were retained for Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny analysis. The available retrieval archive contained 90 PDF instances, including four exact duplicates. Of 86 unique full-text reports screened, 43 met the focused eligibility criteria. The 182-record bibliometric dataset covered 91 sources and 603 unique author names, with recurrent terms involving innovative work behavior, engagement, leadership, psychological empowerment, and knowledge sharing. The focused synthesis identified distinct organizational resources, motivational mechanisms, knowledge processes, and digital capabilities associated with IJP/IWB in the included studies. Much of the primary evidence relied on cross-sectional designs, and the higher-education substream was geographically concentrated. Within the bounded 182-record export, “excellencism” was absent from the searched metadata fields, and no record directly compared Generation Z and Millennials within an IJP/IWB model. The resulting conceptual framework should be interpreted as an evidence-informed synthesis rather than a causally validated model. Future research should improve temporal, multisource, multilevel, and measurement-invariant testing.

items.title: Instruction-Following LLM Agent for Simulating Human Memory Retrieval Process in Household Tasks
items.abstract: Human decision-making in dynamic household environments depends on memory retrieval processes that shape action selection and timing. This paper presents an instruction-following LLM agent as an executable human performance model for simulating memory retrieval behavior in household tasks. The proposed framework integrates memory encoding and decision-making modules with a modified ACT-R base-level activation equation that incorporates environmental entropy and observation duration. The framework was evaluated using human behavioral data from an AI2-THOR-based household task study. When predicting human search times, the modified equation produced lower prediction errors than the conventional ACT-R baseline, reducing MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 11.08%, 5.37%, and 16.00%, respectively. These findings provide preliminary evidence that incorporating context-sensitive retrieval factors may support closer alignment with human search-time behavior in executable LLM-based human performance models.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Into Nursing Care Planning
items.abstract: This methodological study evaluated and compared the content quality and appropriateness of nursing care plans developed by nurses and artificial intelligence (AI) for addressing the psychosocial problems of patients with stomas. Two nursing care plans addressing the psychosocial needs of a patient with a stoma were developed: 1 generated by nurses and 1 generated by an AI system. The content quality and appropriateness of the care plans were independently evaluated by 12 experts, including nursing academics and clinical nurses, using the DISCERN measurement tool. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). The mean DISCERN score of the nurse-generated care plan was significantly higher than that of the AI-generated care plan (P=.008). Inter-rater agreement demonstrated good agreement. The findings indicate that nurse-generated care plans demonstrate superior content quality and overall integrity compared to AI-generated plans. AI-generated care plans exhibit potential as supportive tools in nursing care planning.

items.title: Integrating generative AI with multimodal interaction to inquire into scientific phenomena
items.abstract: This study developed and evaluated two customised generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots designed to provide stepwise guidance for secondary students’ inquiry into scientific phenomena. Biology and physics chatbots were developed using the Predict–Observe–Explain (POE) framework and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to align with Singapore science syllabuses and incorporated segmented video demonstrations. 14 evaluators quantitatively and qualitatively assessed the chatbots in terms of Accuracy, Clarity, Dialogue flow, Ease of use, and Efficiency. Both chatbots were rated positively overall, particularly for Ease of use, Clarity, Efficiency, and Accuracy, while Dialogue flow received lower ratings, especially for the physics chatbot. Qualitative feedback identified needs for stronger scaffolding, better handling of follow-up questions, and additional multimodal support. The findings highlight key design considerations for GenAI-supported scientific inquiry.

items.title: Integrating generative artificial intelligence facilitates faculty interaction network and role transition in a biostatistics curriculum
items.abstract: In a two-year action-research study within an undergraduate biostatistics curriculum for nursing, pharmacy, and medical biotechnology students, we examined how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) facilitates educators to design, supervise, and evaluate learning. Students used GenAI first as a technical tutor and then as a partner in knowledge co-creation in case-based statistical problem-solving. Teachers’ reflection records and 4697 LINE messages during the study period were analyzed using qualitative coding, GenAI-assisted semantic analysis, and social network analysis. Teachers’ roles shifted from knowledge transmitters to facilitators of critical inquiry and human–GenAI co-learning. Overall, faculty communication was dense, reciprocal, and decentralized, whereas GenAI-related discourse was more selective and centralized. GenAI-related ties were less likely to form but, once formed, strongly reciprocal and locally clustered. GenAI integration can catalyze new forms of faculty leadership through expertise sharing and collaborative problem-solving. Intentional structures for cross-disciplinary exchange and reflective faculty development are needed.

items.title: Integrating large language model-generated culturally adapted verbal suggestions into music therapy for university students: A pilot randomized exploratory study
items.abstract: Previous research has suggested that culturally mismatched interventions may cause resistance and reduce the effectiveness of music-based interventions. This pilot randomized exploratory study examined the implementation and preliminary outcomes of a music-based intervention incorporating large language model (LLM)-generated, culturally adapted verbal suggestions among Chinese undergraduate students. A total of 113 participants were randomly assigned to three multicomponent conditions: (1) Chinese film music accompanied by LLM-generated verbal suggestions involving Eastern imagery, (2) a standardized music therapy recording with conventional verbal guidance, or (3) piano music without verbal guidance. Following a 40-minute cognitively demanding task, participants completed pre- and post-intervention measures of state anxiety, positive and negative affect, and heart rate. Baseline-adjusted ANCOVAs showed no group differences in positive affect, F(2, 109) = 1.03, p = .360, ηp2 = .019, or state anxiety, F(2, 109) = 0.68, p = .511, ηp2 = .012. A significant group effect was found for negative affect, F(2, 109) = 4.60, p = .012, ηp2 = .078; the Eastern imagery group had lower adjusted post-intervention scores than both comparison groups (Holm-adjusted ps = .026). Heart rate also differed across groups, F(2, 109) = 10.56, p < .001, ηp2 = .162, with lower adjusted values in the standardized therapy group than in the other two groups. The findings identify potentially meaningful response patterns but do not establish efficacy or the independent effect of culturally adapted verbal suggestions because the conditions differed in musical material and duration. Larger, controlled trials are required. (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07359950).

items.title: Integrating sentiment and contextual information for suicide ideation detection in online social networks: a BERT-BiTCN-sentiment hybrid approach
items.abstract: Background Worldwide, suicide ranks as one of the primary causes of mortality. Taking action and implementing measures to address suicidal thoughts is essential for the well-being of public health. Today, methodologies developed by artificial intelligence serve important functions in the medical field, both as decision-making systems and as sources of information. This observation highlights the increasing integration of machine learning and deep learning into psychiatry, complementing traditional medical practices. Digital social platforms can significantly contribute to the early diagnosis of suicidal tendencies and the implementation of preventive measures. Individuals increasingly express their thoughts and feelings on platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, and Instagram. It has been observed that many individuals struggling with severe psychological disorders express their feelings and reactions on social media platforms. This research aims to early detect suicidal ideation by developing a hybrid model that automatically detects suicide-related posts on online social networks (OSNs). Method First, three datasets were combined to create a new dataset of 254,198 samples. Subsequently, data preprocessing techniques were implemented to diminish the dataset’s size and mitigate noise in the data. Additionally, word embedding techniques, including Term Frequency Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), N-Gram-TF-IDF, and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), were employed during the feature engineering phase. At the same time, the compound sentiment score for each post was computed for integration into the hybrid model. This study developed the BERT-Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional Network (BiTCN)-Sentiment (BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment) model by integrating BERT’s capacity to extract contextual meaning from textual data with BiTCN’s proficiency in capturing bidirectional relationships in sequential data. The BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment hybrid model proposed in this study was used for the first time to detect suicidal ideation in social networks. Results The experimental studies demonstrated that the BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment model attained superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 95.45%, precision of 95.45%, recall of 95.45%, and an F-score of 95.45%. The Multilingual BERT model achieved 94.88% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, ranking second among the models. Moreover, the A Lite BERT (ALBERT), MentalBERT, BERT-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), BERT-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and BERT models attained comparable results. The TF-IDF-LightGBM model proved to be the most proficient among the machine learning models, attaining 90.60% in accuracy, precision, recall, and F-score. This study culminated in the development of a successful hybrid model capable of early detection of posts indicative of suicidal tendencies among users on online social networks.

items.title: Integrating technology anxiety into the TPB-TAM framework to examine AI adoption intention in hospital HRM: a study of Chinese healthcare professionals
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can empower healthcare professionals to make data-driven decisions and streamline administrative tasks in hospital human resource management (HRM). However, it is vital to understand their perceptions towards AI for seamless implementation in practice. Therefore, the study aimed to assess the role of technology anxiety within an integrated framework combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to better understand adoption intentions in this high-stakes context. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 547 healthcare professionals working in hospitals across China. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling, including confirmatory factor analysis, path analysis, and bootstrap mediation testing. Multi-group structural equation modeling was also used to compare healthcare professionals with different levels of AI familiarity. The integrated model explained 49.4% of the variance in behavioral intention, and all twelve hypothesized paths were statistically significant. Technology anxiety was negatively associated with perceived ease of use (β = -0.553, p < 0.001), perceived behavioral control (β = -0.371, p < 0.001), attitude (β = -0.339, p < 0.001), and subjective norms (β = -0.451, p < 0.001), and it was also associated with behavioral intention through multiple indirect pathways. Multi-group analysis showed that the association between perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness was stronger among professionals with low AI familiarity, while the remaining paths remained stable across groups. AI adoption intention in hospital HRM appears to involve more than rational evaluations of usefulness and ease of use. Emotional states, such as technology anxiety, also play a role. Reducing technology anxiety and improving ease of use for users with lower AI familiarity are therefore important steps for promoting AI adoption intention. These findings highlight the value of addressing emotional factors alongside cognitive beliefs when introducing AI tools in healthcare organizations.

items.abstract: Purpose: This study is focused on capability enhancement for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven digital twins of warehouses, logistics hubs, and supply chain networks, which can be created within the metaverse. Integration of real-time data from Internet of Things (IoT) devices can update sophisticated systems which implemented new and emerging technologies, allowing for virtual monitoring, predictive maintenance, and process optimization. This study will provide insights into what capabilities can be enhanced for a seamless integration and implementation of this technology. Methodology: This is a structured literature review of 36 articles that emphasize on the capabilities that are implementing this technology and creating a more resilient ecosystem. The structured literature review would follow the PRISMA flow method to shortlist the best-fit articles for this study. Findings: The best-fit articles would be used to create a conceptual framework that would help the development of the integration of AI agents in the metaverse ecosystem and enhance the capabilities to make a resilient organization. The strategies that can help in intelligent planning and simulation would be utilized to create a competitive advantage for the firms. Conclusion: The fusion of AI agents and the metaverse marks a transformative leap in supply chain logistics, aligning with the human-centric vision of Industry 5.0. This integration not only enhances operational efficiency but also promotes a seamless collaboration between humans and intelligent systems within immersive virtual environments. Originality: The enhancement in capabilities is an essential part of the implementation of this technology. This is specifically targeted to create more resilient firms and an overall positive firm performance to survive in Industry 5.0.

items.title: Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis Incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Identifies Putative Pathogenic HNF1B Missense Variants Associated with HNF1B-MODY
items.abstract: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 5 (MODY5 or HNF1B-MODY) is a rare form of diabetes caused by variants in HNF1B. Patients with MODY5 exhibit high blood sugar levels and symptoms commonly associated with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1D, T2D), along with kidney and pancreatic issues. Nonetheless, diagnosis, treatment and management approaches depend on specific genotype–phenotype associations. Interpretation of HNF1B missense variants remains challenging because of conflicting classifications and limited clinical evidence. This study aimed to improve the interpretation of HNF1B missense variants with conflicting evidence regarding pathogenicity and thereby advance the genetic and molecular understanding of HNF1B-MODY. An integrative computational approach combining artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and conventional bioinformatic tools, including Panther, SIFT, SNAP2, Meta-SNP, PhD-SNP, PolyPhen-2, and AlphaMissense, was used to identify deleterious missense variants in the HNF1B gene. The variants were further processed to determine their effects on protein conformation, stability, function, and conservation across species. Among 982 reported variants retrieved from the ClinVar database, 368 were classified as missense. Only 47 missense variants were labelled with conflicting classification and reported with clinical uncertainty. Consensus analysis by all tools identified five candidate variants (His153Arg, Asn298Asp, Arg303His, Lys305Glu, and Val458Gly), representing 10.6% (5/47) as potentially pathogenic. AlphaMissense classified all five as likely pathogenic, with scores ranging from 0.8921 to 1.000. Secondary structure analysis indicates that the His153Arg, Asn298Asp, Arg303His, and Lys305Glu variants are in the helical region, while the Val458Gly variant is located within the coil region. Interestingly, all five filtered variants are predicted by the I-Mutant and MuPro tools to reduce protein stability. The three-dimensional (3D) protein structures were constructed using the Deep Learning-Based Iterative Threading Assembly Refinement (D-I-TASSER) tool and visualised by UCSF Chimera. Structural modelling showed similarity between the mutant and wild-type models, with RMSD values ranging from 0.77 to 1.36 Å. The multiple sequence alignments show that amino acids at variant sites across all variants are highly conserved among species. These findings show that combining traditional bioinformatics with artificial intelligence and machine learning improves the interpretation of HNF1B missense variants with clinical uncertainty. Integrating computational predictions with structural, evolutionary, and clinical data provides a framework for prioritising variants for further functional and clinical investigation.

items.title: Intelligent Circuit Design: Exploring Artificial Intelligence for Logic Gate Synthesis and Optimization
items.abstract: Modern integrated circuits contain billions of logic gates, while thermal and sub-micron parasitic limits make every design decision more expensive. Classical logic synthesis relies on deterministic minimization and hand-engineered heuristics that struggle to balance Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) at the same time. This paper reviews how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can support logic gate synthesis in Electronic Design Automation (EDA): Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for circuit representation and early PPA prediction, Reinforcement Learning (RL) for restructuring And-Inverter Graphs (AIGs) and Majority-Inverter Graphs (MIGs), and Transformer-based Large Circuit Models (LCMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for hardware generation. Building on the survey of Astillero (2026), it proposes a verification-first hybrid framework in which learned models suggest optimizations and formal equivalence checking guarantees correctness, together with an experimental protocol for evaluating it against classical flows.

items.title: Intelligent Robots for Elderly Care: Categories, Application Scenarios, and Challenges
items.abstract: Aging populations have increased the demand for intelligent, personalized, and emotionally supportive elderly care services. Traditional care models often face limitations such as high labor costs, insufficient service continuity, and limited emotional support. Deep learning-driven elderly care robots provide a promising solution by integrating perception, decision-making, human-robot interaction, and adaptive service functions. This paper reviews the major categories of intelligent elderly care robots, including rehabilitation robots, nursing robots, and companion robots. It further discusses their application scenarios in home care, nursing homes, and community-based care. Existing studies show that deep learning, machine vision, multimodal sensing, and large language models can improve motion assistance, health monitoring, emotional interaction, and personalized companionship. However, several challenges remain, including technical reliability, data privacy, ethical risks, high deployment costs, and user acceptance among older adults. Future development should focus on lightweight models, multimodal fusion, privacy-preserving learning, and human-centered design. Intelligent elderly care robots should not replace human caregivers, but should support them in providing safer, more efficient, and more compassionate care.

items.title: Intelligent Technologies as Proponents of Global Development and Sustainability: An Approach Based on India's Digital Infrastructure
items.abstract: The seventeen core goals of the UN's 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development demand the need for collective action along social, economic, and environmental fronts. Artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, along with cloud/edge computing are notable examples of intelligent technologies and also regarded as facilitators of this agenda. However, the literature that discusses these technologies tends to interpret technology and policy goals in isolation, thus paying inconsistent attention across the seventeen goals and hardly establishing its claims on the realities of any one nation. This paper aims to bridge that gap. It presents a taxonomy of intelligent technologies, aligns them onto a particular segment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) involving infrastructure, human well-being, education, energy and climate, disparities, and sustainable cities, and foundations that connecting on case studies from smart city initiatives and digital public infrastructure projects in India. With the goal to lead future technology-for-development research, the research study builds on this depiction and recommends a four-layer conceptual framework: Infrastructure, Intelligence, Trust, and Impact. It draws its conclusion by inspecting the obstacles that challenge this optimism, such as the digital gap, data privacy, a bias in the algorithm and environmental impact of computation itself, before emphasizing federated and privacy-preserving techniques as a feasible direction for further research. Keywords: artificial intelligence; federated learning; smart cities; Internet of things; Sustainable Development Goals; Digital Public Infrastructure

items.title: Interpersonal Competence as a Dimension of Global Competence and its Relationship with Academic Motivation among Undergraduate Students
items.abstract: Global competence is integral to higher education because students need the knowledge, skills, and attitudes to learn effectively and participate in an interconnected world. Interpersonal competence is one part of it: the ability to cooperate and communicate with people from different cultural and educational backgrounds. This study examined the relationship between interpersonal competence (Skills) and undergraduate students' academic motivation, using a quantitative correlational design. Data were collected from 1,200 undergraduate students in the Education departments of three universities in Lahore. The Skills dimension of the Global Competence Scale (Liu et al., 2020) measured interpersonal competence, and the Academic Motivation Scale (AMS) measured academic motivation. Pearson product-moment correlations were computed between skills and intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and amotivation. Skills showed statistically significant moderate positive correlations with intrinsic motivation (r = 0.409, p < 0.001) and extrinsic motivation (r = 0.364, p < .001), and a statistically significant but very weak negative correlation with amotivation (r = −0.133, p < 0.001). Students with stronger interpersonal skills therefore tended to report higher intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, while the association with amotivation was small.

items.title: Interpersonal Emotion Regulation in Middle Childhood: From Cognitive Capacity to Context-Sensitive Regulation
items.abstract: Interpersonal emotion regulation (IER) requires individuals to understand another person’s emotional state and adapt regulatory decisions to interpersonal goals and situational demands. Across four linked studies, the present research examined age-related patterns, cognitive and social-cognitive correlates, contextual modulation, and individual differences in context sensitivity in children aged 8–10 years. IER was assessed using vignette-based strategy ratings, executive-function and social-cognitive measures, and experimental manipulations of regulatory goals and demands. Across the observed age range, increasing age was associated with greater cognitive and affective engagement and lower avoidance and co-rumination, whereas distraction and suppression showed no significant age associations. Executive function, empathy, and theory of mind were systematically associated with greater adaptive and lower maladaptive IER. Children also altered their regulatory decisions as social goals and regulatory demands changed. Person-by-context analyses showed selective effects: general cognitive-control capacity moderated responsiveness to regulatory goals, whereas social cognition moderated demand-related variation in cognitive engagement. Together, the findings suggest that IER in middle childhood involves not only developing regulatory capacities but also coordinating those capacities with the goals and demands of interpersonal situations.

items.title: Interpreting Machine Learning Predictions with SHAP and LIME for Transparent Decision Making
items.abstract: Machine learning models increasingly influence critical decisions across diverse domains, yet their complex architectures often operate as black boxes, obscuring the rationale behind predictions and limiting stakeholder trust. This research demonstrates a comprehensive, reproducible workflow for applying explainable artificial intelligence techniques to interpret Random Forest classifier decisions using publicly available data and standard computational resources. The study implements and compares two leading explanation methods, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), on the Titanic survival prediction task to evaluate their consistency and practical utility. The methodology encompasses automated data preprocessing, model training with regularization to prevent overfitting, and systematic generation of both global and local explanations through multiple visualization formats. Results reveal exceptional agreement between explanation methods, with Spearman rank correlation of 0.918 and Pearson correlation of 0.982 for feature importance values. Both techniques consistently identified passenger sex as the dominant predictive feature, contributing approximately 15.4% and 12.5% of model decisions respectively, followed by passenger class and fare. The Random Forest model achieved 84.5% test set ROC-AUC with controlled overfitting (0.040 ROC-AUC gap between training and test sets) while maintaining interpretable complexity through architectural constraints. The implementation executes efficiently on CPU hardware within minutes, eliminating computational barriers to XAI adoption. This work establishes that current explainability techniques can provide reliable, consistent insights into ensemble model decisions while remaining accessible to researchers and practitioners with limited computational resources.

items.title: Intuitive Robot Programming
items.abstract: The introduction of robots in SMEs requires a drastic reconsideration of existing programming techniques and interfaces. The growing versatility of the market essentially demands the robots to be re-programmed frequently, calling for interfaces that are intuitive enough to require no robotic expertise, yet flexible enough to meet industrial needs. Rather than limiting the intervention of the workers, the technology should empower them to take control over the machine. Only then, the human-machine complementarity can be leveraged, combining the efficiency of automation with the flexibility of human work. Ergonomics and human factors are critical to the development of these new programming interfaces, which should typically be developed and tested in a cyclic fashion with the end-users. In this chapter, we highlight the differences between easy-to-learn and easy-to-use interfaces, as well as the differences between interfaces targeting naive/casual users and interfaces targeting expert/professional workers. We discuss the design of robot programming interfaces based on a user-centric perspective. The research developments in this project target different methods to collect demonstrations (including tracked devices and kinesthetic teaching), different graphical user interfaces (including block-based and timeline representations), and different approaches to augmented reality (including tablets/smartphones, headsets or actuated projection devices). Through this multi-modular approach, we aim at providing workers with the most natural way possible to interact with the robot depending on the task or their preferences.
